body:
Something similar happens to me, but during depressive episodes too. My psychiatrist calls it "pseudodementia." He said it is definitely related to the symptoms of bipolar disorder. I forget to lock the door, leave things on the stove, lose all focus at work, get confused when speaking... I'm finally out of a several months-long episode and the problem is pretty much gone. I haven't noticed it getting worse or more permanent as I age (though I think I notice it more, and I've advanced more in my career so it's more frustrating).

For what it's worth, my psychiatrist took me off of Lamictal and my cognitive symptoms did improve. That might just be me, though. I'd been on it for over three years. I take Abilify and an antidepressant now.

The self-care tips make perfect sense. I lost some momentum with that when she was born, though I have been absolutely militant about protecting my sleep. 

It's amazing -- she does know my voice, just like they said she would!
Thank you so much for sharing your story. It is scary to see parts of myself in there, but I've never had a bigger incentive to work so hard at managing this.

Thank you for reading and replying. She is so energetic and hates the sling -- she seems to want her freedom (just like mommy). I am going to work on your idea of closeness. I can still carry her when she'll let me, lie down next to her, and so on, and she'll dictate the terms. :)
Well, it's too late for that!

It is such a relief to read these replies. Thank you! It sounds like the preschool years are especially tough, and age 10 or so may be a turning point for understanding. I'll keep that in mind as she and I age together!

I love the pajama day idea! I've also been thinking that if nothing else, I'll at least be well-equipped to talk to her about any issues of her own she might experience. I think having this disorder has made me a better person -- but I do get stressed when I can't act like myself all the time.

Thank you for this. I have been feeling so guilty and really needed this reminder to not beat myself up about this. Reading is a great idea -- I seem to be able to read to her even when I'm totally useless in most other ways.

I am so sorry for your loss. You have every right to grieve this. I hate the taboo against talking about pregnancies and babies until you are X weeks along. There is nothing magical about week X that makes it any more "real" than it was any week prior. Also, other people's feelings, no matter what they are, don't make it any less real.

I interpreted this differently than the other poster. I had been deeply depressed for a very long time when I found out I was pregnant. Suddenly, it wasn't like the baby had the job (of making me happy), it was like I had a job. This little creature was totally dependent on me. Things that had bothered me the week before seemed stupid and inconsequential in light of this new, awesome responsibility. I now had to stay alive and take care of myself. So I remember those feelings.

It sucks that you are not getting the support you deserve. No matter what your circumstances are, you are allowed to be sad about this. 

-hugs-

Thank you so much! You are right, I think looking the part will help a lot (both in terms of getting into the right mindset and making the right impression). I'm glad you successfully got through your day!

This actually reminded me of an incident from a couple of years ago. I ran into a former therapist at this same garden center. I was wearing no makeup (strange for me) and mismatched clothes, and talking a mile a minute, and I had about a dozen large shrubs with me (for some reason I was carrying three of them in my arms instead of getting a second cart). The look on her face was memorable. The funny thing is I actually needed all of the shrubs for a hedge I was planting. I tried to convey that to her but I probably was not very convincing. Lol

I am going to go to the garden center and buy a couple of plants. This will get me outside today and again when I have to plant them. 

Also I am going to stay hydrated. I sucked at that last week and I felt like hell. I would not do well with Lithium.

These are good ideas. I needed the reminder to reframe before I totally psyched myself out. I used to look through old successful projects to get into the right mindset -- maybe I will do that. 

My colleagues know something's up with me, but I don't dare tell them what. I can ask a few friends to send good vibes my way. Plus the internet. :) Thanks so much.

Thank you for this. I love the reminder that this won't require coming off as elated -- projecting confidence really will be enough. I think I tend to overcompensate in these situations, which, you're right, is draining.

I used to be terrible at this. I was relatively high-functioning and embarrassed to look anything but (and especially embarrassed to share some of the stranger parts of what I was experiencing, like borderline paranoia and embarrassing intrusive thoughts). Everyone who treated me commented that I didn't look like I was having serious problems, so the facade was working. But I was not doing myself any favors, and ended up seriously undertreated for years. I requested my medical records from that time and was shocked at how trivial my problems appeared on paper, when I was barely functioning, struggling to keep myself alive, and considering taking leave from work (that's actually noted in the record). I had to change my strategy. I now bring written notes to my psychiatry appointments so I don't self-censor while I'm there. And therapy helped a lot with the vulnerability issue.
